The tool name was also corrected (get-library-docs -> query-docs) and the params renamed (context7CompatibleLibraryId/topic -> libraryId/query). The +95 bytes is the longer-but-accurate mechanism description; it is the literal fix for the mis-attribution, not incidental prose growth, and the rationale must be correct because agents read it to decide when to fall back to the CLI. #3021 amendment: branch allow-list regex widened to accept worktree-wf_* (Workflow backend naming) alongside agent-*/worktree-agent-*. — #3210 append: the unmet-<precondition> branch now reports the returned checkpoint with **Gate:** blocking-human (both auto-mode bypass layers key on that gate; without it auto-mode silently auto-approved the checkpoint with a synthetic 'approved'), the auto-mode human-verify rule names precondition-unmet checkpoints as exempt, and checkpoint_return_format's Gate line notes precondition-unmet checkpoints report blocking-human; +134 bytes, still under the 49152 cap. — #3576 append: bare `references/<name>.md` cites repaired to the canonical `gsd-core/references/<name>.md` form (+18 bytes, 2 cite(s) × 9). Dead-pointer fix; no content change. — #3299 append: the tracer feedback gate's interactive branch now consults HUMAN_VERIFY_MODE instead of keying on auto-mode alone, and <auto_mode_detection> gains the config read for it. The branch is written as an explicit ordered precedence chain — (1) gate="blocking-human" STOPs, (2) end-of-phase + automated-only <verify> re-runs it with failure HALTing and never becoming an approvable checkpoint, (3) everything else STOPs — because an earlier revision phrased it as 'continues on success; otherwise return a checkpoint', which grammatically routed a FAILING tracer into a checkpoint a user could approve and then expand onto a broken slice (caught in peer review). The branch deliberately avoids the literal tokens 'Rule' and a bare '3' on the same line: tests/package-legitimacy-gate.test.cjs locates its RULE 3 section by first-line token match, and an earlier revision numbering the branches (1)/(2)/(3) while citing 'deviation Rule 1' hijacked that window and broke the package-install exclusion assertion. Deliberately near-net-neutral (+129 bytes) rather than carrying the full rule: this file is LARGE tier in tests/agent-size-budget.test.cjs against a 49152-byte hard cap and had only 154 bytes of headroom at upstream/next@2b20b7e2. The branch rule and the read stay inline (the executor must act on them without a further hop); the precedence table and the --default rationale live in gsd-core/references/checkpoints.md, which <checkpoint_protocol> already @-imports — so no new file is loaded and no eager-import relocation was introduced. Room was reclaimed from non-operative prose in the same block: one autonomous-branch rationale sentence ('Pouring more layers onto a broken foundation...'), the 'the leading thin end-to-end slice' gloss on the task-type heading (CONTEXT.md's glossary is the canonical definition and is asserted there), and two redundant parentheticals. Every assertion in the pre-existing executor contract in tests/tracer-bullet.test.cjs still matches. Final size 49127 — 25 bytes of headroom, disclosed because the next contributor who needs room here must extract lazily rather than add prose.
